facts.t: Parliament sits for half as many days as it once did
facts.d: The Lok Sabha met around 127 days a year in the 1950s. It now manages under 60 to 70. The volume of legislation has not fallen correspondingly — what has fallen is the time available to examine it.

Around 60 to 70% of Bills were referred to departmentally related standing committees in the 14th and 15th Lok Sabhas. In the 17th it was roughly 16%. The committee stage is where clause-by-clause examination happens, and it is being skipped.

facts.t: Bribing an MP is no longer protected by privilege
facts.d: P. V. Narasimha Rao (1998) had held that an MP who took a bribe and then voted was immune from prosecution. Sita Soren (2024) overturned it — a seven-judge bench holding that corruption cannot be shielded by parliamentary privilege.

bank.q: With reference to the roles of a parliamentarian, consider the following statements:
s: Financial control derives from the Commons principle of no taxation without representation.
MPLADS provides ₹5 crore per year per MP.
Scrutiny of delegated legislation is a deliberative rather than legislative function.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Scrutinising delegated legislation is classified as a legislative function.

bank.q: Approximately what proportion of Bills was referred to standing committees in the 17th Lok Sabha?
bank.e: About 16%, against 60 to 70% in the 14th and 15th Lok Sabhas — the sharpest measure of declining legislative scrutiny.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct about the 18th Lok Sabha?
o: There are 74 women MPs, about 14% of the House
The average age of MPs is around 56
Fewer than half of MPs have undergraduate education
bank.e: About 78% have at least an undergraduate degree.

bank.as: The anti-defection law weakens executive accountability.
bank.rs: Legislators must vote as the party whip directs, which converts them into party instruments rather than independent scrutineers.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. It also lets MPs deflect voter accountability by blaming the whip.

bank.q: Match List I (country) with List II (practice relevant to India):
pairs: 2. MPs may break a three-line whip on conscience issues
3. Deputy Speaker roles rotate across parties
4. Permanent committees with large expert staff
bank.e: The UK's calibrated whip, American committee staffing, German rapporteurs, and Canadian rotation of deputy speakerships.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about parliamentary committees:
s: Departmentally related standing committee attendance averaged around 49% between 2009 and 2014.
Their one-year tenure impedes the accumulation of expertise.
Public Accounts Committee recommendations are legally binding on the government.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. PAC recommendations are not binding, though around 80% are accepted.

bank.q: In Sita Soren (2024) the Supreme Court held that:
o: Parliamentary privilege extends to accepting a bribe for a vote
There is no immunity from prosecution for bribery relating to a vote or speech
Privileges must be codified by Parliament within a year
Speaker's decisions under the Tenth Schedule are final
bank.e: It overturned P. V. Narasimha Rao (1998), holding that privilege cannot shield corruption.

bank.q: All of the following are proposed structural reforms EXCEPT:
o: Mandatory committee referral of non-urgent Bills
Extending standing committee tenure beyond one year
bank.e: The proposal is to confine whips to confidence and money matters — as recommended by the 170th Law Commission and the NCRWC — not to abolish them.

bank.q: The disqualification of twenty Delhi MLAs in 2018 concerned:
o: Office of profit through Parliamentary Secretary posts
bank.e: Office of profit under Articles 102(1)(a) and 191(1)(a) — an area whose ambiguity remains unresolved.

bank.q: With reference to disruptions in Parliament, consider the following:
s: Sessions frequently run at under 50% of scheduled time.
In 2016 the Rajya Sabha could not take up the Finance and Appropriation Bills amid protests.
Question Hour washouts strengthen executive accountability by forcing written replies.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Question Hour washouts erode oversight — they do not substitute for it.

bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
items: Sita Soren overturns the earlier position
P. V. Narasimha Rao is decided
Keisham Meghachandra Singh on time-bound adjudication
bank.e: The Tenth Schedule via the 52nd Amendment (1985) → P. V. Narasimha Rao (1998) → Keisham Meghachandra Singh (2020) → Sita Soren (2024).

bank.as: Electoral incentives push MPs towards constituency work over legislative scrutiny.
bank.rs: Visible MPLADS delivery is more electorally rewarding than committee attendance.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the structural tension between the representative and deliberative functions of the office.
